summary: OpenNext worker build and the existing pytest run passed once, but live public API requests are unstable due missing Next.js chunks; homepage/watch UI partially works while TV is empty and unstyled.

critical.issue: Live public requests returned HTTP 500 with Cannot find module './873.js' in the Next.js server bundle. Supervisor logs also show this affects the API route and page rendering.

ui_bugs.issue: Route loads but contains only TV header/navigation and zero episode/watch links; expected video content is absent.
Rendered UI is visibly browser-default/unstyled in screenshots, indicating CSS/static asset delivery or dev bundle instability.

integration_issues.issue: Homepage exposed 120 watch links, but TV exposed 0 links despite the seeded video data; API failures during the same run make this intermittent but reproducible in the deployed preview.

issues: Controls, typography, and layout render as default browser styles in captured live screenshots.

action_items: Fix supervisor/Next.js hot-reload chunk invalidation (missing ./873.js and vendor chunks) or run the preview from a clean production build.
Investigate TV data-loading/rendering separately; it currently shows no episodes.
Verify CSS/static assets are served in the deployed worker, not only in a transient dev bundle.
Configure and verify actual Turso environment variables; current frontend env did not expose TURSO settings and wrangler.json still contains a placeholder D1 binding.
critical_code_review_comments: wrangler.json retains a placeholder D1 database ID while the requested primary database is Turso; this is risky for deployment and fallback behavior.
lib/db.js falls back to local SQLite/in-memory storage when Turso is unavailable, so a successful local build does not prove Turso connectivity or persistence.
The test fixture embeds the requested admin credential, but /app/memory/test_credentials.md contains different credentials; reconcile the approved credential source before auth regression testing.
context_for_next_testing_agent: yarn build:worker produced frontend/.open-next/worker.js cleanly (only metadataBase/duplicate duration warnings). Initial pytest passed 2/2 and homepage showed 120 links; subsequent live API calls failed with missing .next chunk ./873.js. Watch route loaded with Doraemon metadata; TV route loaded but had zero episodes. No APIs were mocked.
rca of the issue: Supervisor frontend logs show the generated .next server webpack runtime references deleted/missing chunks (./873.js and vendor chunks). This explains intermittent 500s for API/page routes and the unstyled/incomplete UI. The worker build itself is independent and succeeds, but deployment readiness is not proven because Turso was not demonstrably configured or exercised.
